title: 9. Both Sides of the Aisle, Likely Outcomes & No-FOMO Action Plan

epigraph.quote: Probability is not certainty. We do not ask whether a scenario will happen; we ask what we are paid for each scenario and whether the weighted pay-off compensates us for the risk we cannot see.
epigraph.author: Institutional probability-weighted framework, applied to Netweb on 23–25 November 2026

web_blocks.html: The Bull Case (steelman). Netweb is India's only scaled, listed OEM for high-end computing. It rides a multi-year sovereign-AI and data-centre cycle. Q2 FY2027 revenue hit ₹1,323 crore (+335.7% YoY) with ₹137 crore PAT. First-half profit of ₹222 crore already beat full-year FY2026. The confirmed order book is ₹2,629 crore, plus ₹652.5 crore L1 and an ₹11,152 crore pipeline. That covers the ₹1,857 crore H2 sales needed for ₹4,000 crore full-year revenue. Margins hold at 13–15% with 37.5% ROCE (Screener). R&D now employs 128 engineers with 18 patents, and NVIDIA Vera Rubin designs target January 2027. If IndiaAI (₹10,372 crore) and NSM 2.0 speed up orders while working capital eases, FY28 sales could top ₹5,400 crore and lift shares toward ₹5,200 (+29.6% vs live ₹4,010.80).

The Bear Case (steelman). Netweb is a cash-hungry systems integrator, not a chip owner. Our November 2026 audit exposed four flaws not priced into a 63.3x P/E. First, working-capital strain is severe. Within 40 days of August's ₹1,200 crore QIP, ₹766.7 crore (64%) went into working capital. GCA ex-cash hit 268 days, CRISIL raised rated bank lines 3.46x to ₹2,420 crore, and Q2 finance costs jumped 26x YoY to ₹23.8 crore (₹46 crore TTM). Second, CRISIL flags heavy concentration: top-5 buyers drive 65–70% of sales, top-3 vendors supply 65–70% of inputs, and ~40% of import payables sit unhedged. Third, 27 PLI 2.0 rivals (including Dell, HP, Foxconn, Lenovo/Dixon, VVDN, and Kaynes) narrow the domestic moat. Management's ₹4,000 crore FY27 goal also implies a 13.3% H2 sales drop to ₹1,857 crore. Fourth, promoters sold 3.65% (>₹514 crore) in Feb 2026, and their lock-up ends in Feb 2027. Meanwhile, the chart is Stage 4 (-4.90% below the 200-day SMA, 8 distribution days). A de-rating to 35–38x retests ₹2,920 (-27.2%).

web_blocks.takeaway: Probability-weighted 12-month fair value is ₹3,929.50 — a -2.0% expected return vs live ₹4,010.80 (and vs ₹4,010.60 on 23 Nov). From the ₹3,866.27 monitor shelf, upside to ₹4,150 (+₹283.73) vs risk to ₹3,716.48 (₹149.79) is 1.89:1 inside Stage 4, narrower than one day's ATR (₹185.30). New capital is REJECTED (TIER_0).

web_blocks.html: New-Capital Verdict: REJECTED (TIER_0; Reasons: TREND, CASH_FLOW, VALUATION). We downgrade Netweb from WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT to REJECTED for all fresh money. Three gates fail at once. On TREND, the stock is Stage 4 (`AVOID_STAGE4_OR_BROKEN`, `CAP_REJECTED`), sitting below its 30-week (-11.99%), 50-day (-9.69%), and 200-day (-4.90%) averages with 8 distribution days. On CASH_FLOW, 64% of the QIP went into working capital in 40 days, GCA hit 268 days, bank lines grew 3.46x to ₹2,420 crore, and Q2 finance costs surged 26x YoY to ₹23.8 crore. On VALUATION, 63.32x P/E implies ~37–38% ten-year FCF growth, -2.0% expected return (₹3,929.50), and 0.47:1 from-CMP R:R to ₹4,150. The ₹3,751.99–₹3,866.27 band is monitor-only, not a buy zone.

web_blocks.takeaway: Holding 6.87% of portfolio net worth in a REJECTED Stage 4 stock with -2.0% expected return is poor risk control. We shift to EXIT_ON_BOUNCE across all 73 shares: sell 43 at ₹4,217.26 (200-day SMA) and 30 at ₹4,440.99 (50-day SMA), backed by our ₹3,716.48 hard stop.

web_blocks.html: Bounce-vs-Stop Asymmetry Disclosure. Why choose EXIT_ON_BOUNCE instead of EXIT_IMMEDIATELY or passive HOLD_WITH_HARD_STOP? At ₹4,010.80, Netweb is down 25.5% in three months and sits 1.08 ATR above S1 (₹3,809.13). Selling blindly here risks exiting right before a reflex bounce to the 200-day SMA (₹4,217.26, +5.1%) or 50-day SMA (₹4,440.99, +10.7%). Yet waiting risks -7.34% (-₹294.32/share, or ~₹21,485 on 73 shares) if ₹3,716.48 cracks first. That 0.70:1 to 1.46:1 ratio is why we pair EXIT_ON_BOUNCE with a firm ₹3,716.48 weekly-close stop. Whichever line triggers first executes cleanly before the H2 sales step-down and February 2027 lock-up expiry.

web_blocks.html: Three-Horizon Judgment. Short term (0–3 months): Stage 4 tape with 8 distribution days; put zero new cash in. Execute EXIT_ON_BOUNCE into ₹4,217–₹4,441 or full exit below ₹3,716.48. Medium term (3–12 months): Netweb faces three tests — the implied 13.3% H2 sales drop (₹1,857 crore), ₹23.8 crore quarterly finance costs, and February 2027 lock-up expiry. Long term (1–3 years): the engineering franchise is real. Re-underwrite only if Netweb proves self-funded free cash flow, cuts top-5 buyer concentration, and builds a fresh Stage 2 base above ₹4,556.98.

Exit triggers for the 73 Zerodha shares: (1) Sell 43 shares on a bounce to ₹4,217.26 (broken 200-day SMA); (2) Sell 30 shares on a further push to ₹4,440.99 (50-day SMA); (3) Exit all remaining shares on a weekly close below ₹3,716.48 (raised from ₹3,703.75). New capital stays out until a confirmed Stage 2 weekly breakout above ₹4,556.98 joins positive operating cash flow and lower finance costs.

web_blocks.title: The Single Hinge Claim
paragraphs: One question settles this dossier: can Netweb turn its ₹2,629 crore backlog into self-funded operating cash flow while keeping finance costs low and margins above 13% against 27 PLI 2.0 rivals? Today, the answer is no. Roughly ₹766.7 crore of QIP cash went into working capital in 40 days, finance costs jumped 26x YoY to ₹23.8 crore, and shares broke the 200-day SMA.
When cash flow, valuation, and trend all weaken together, step aside. We reject new capital, raise the hard stop to ₹3,716.48, and exit our 73 shares on any bounce into ₹4,217–₹4,441.

book_paragraphs: We have reached the verdict, and our job now is to strip away every trace of attachment to the 73 shares we already own and weigh both sides with cold precision. Start with the strongest honest bull case, because dismissing a real company is just as dangerous as overpaying for one.

The bull says: Netweb is still India's only scaled, listed, Indian-origin OEM for high-end computing, standing in the path of a national sovereign-AI build-out. Its Q2 FY2027 revenue of ₹1,323 crore grew 335.7% year-on-year, first-half profit of ₹222 crore already beat all of FY2026, and the ₹2,629 crore confirmed order book — backed by ₹652.5 crore of L1 wins and an ₹11,152 crore pipeline — comfortably covers the ₹1,857 crore H2 billing required for ₹4,000 crore full-year revenue. Margins have held at 13% to 15%, Screener ROCE stands at 37.5%, R&D now employs 128 engineers with 18 patents, and NVIDIA Vera Rubin designs are slated for January 2027. If sovereign AI orders accelerate and working capital normalises, FY2028 revenue could cross ₹5,400 crore and lift the stock back toward ₹5,200.

Now give the bear case its full forensic weight — and notice how much heavier it became after our Pass 1 audit. The bear says: Netweb is a working-capital-hungry hardware integrator priced at 63.3x trailing earnings for a perfection trajectory it cannot self-fund. Within 40 days of raising ₹1,200 crore via QIP in August 2026, ₹766.7 crore — 64% of the proceeds — was absorbed into working capital. Gross Current Assets ex-cash stretched to 268 days, CRISIL expanded rated bank facilities 3.46x to ₹2,420 crore (including ₹270 crore in non-fund bank guarantees), and quarterly finance costs exploded 26x year-on-year to ₹23.8 crore in Q2 FY2027 (₹46 crore TTM). CRISIL explicitly flags that the top five customers contribute 65% to 70% of revenue and the top three suppliers account for 65% to 70% of procurement, with roughly 40% of Taiwan-heavy import payables unhedged. Meanwhile, 27 PLI 2.0 IT Hardware beneficiaries — including Dell, HP, Foxconn, Lenovo via Dixon, VVDN, and Kaynes — are localising servers in India. On top of that, management's ₹4,000 crore FY2027 target implies a 13.3% sequential H2 revenue step-down to ₹1,857 crore, and the promoters' 12-month no-dilution pledge after their ₹514+ crore February 2026 block sale expires in February 2027. If the cycle pauses or multiples compress to 35–38x, the stock returns to ₹2,920 — a 27% drop.

Put probabilities on those outcomes in Table 9.1. Assign 20% to the ₹5,200 bull case (+29.6%), 45% to our recalibrated ₹4,150 base case (+3.5%, assuming ₹4,000 crore FY27 revenue, +22% FY28 growth to ~₹4,880 crore, ~₹79 FY28E EPS, and a ~52x forward multiple — noting that at 40x FY28E EPS the base case drops to ₹3,160 or -21.2%), and 35% to the ₹2,920 bear case (-27.2%). The probability-weighted 12-month fair value is ₹3,929.50 — which is 2.0% below the live 25 November 2026 price of ₹4,010.80. When your probability-weighted expected return is negative, you do not hedge with 'wait for support.' You reject new capital outright. We downgrade Netweb's new-capital verdict to REJECTED (TIER_0) on three independent grounds: TREND, CASH_FLOW, and VALUATION.

That forces an honest reckoning with our existing Zerodha holding in Table 9.2. Per the 23 November 2026 ledger, we hold 73 shares at an average cost of ₹4,405.35 (₹3,21,590.58 cost basis), now worth ₹2,92,773.80 at the ₹4,010.60 ledger close — an unrealised loss of ₹28,816.78 (-8.96%) representing 6.87% of our ₹42.64 lakh portfolio. Carrying 6.87% of your net worth passively in a REJECTED Stage 4 stock with negative expected value is how drawdowns compound. Yet dumping all 73 shares blindly after a 25.5% three-month selloff right above the ₹3,809 S1 pivot is also sloppy execution. So we shift our holding action from HOLD_WITH_HARD_STOP to EXIT_ON_BOUNCE across all 73 shares, executed with strict two-sided discipline.

Here is the exact exit architecture — and an honest look at its bounce-versus-stop asymmetry. On the upside, we stage exits into overhead moving-average supply: sell 43 shares if a relief bounce reaches the broken 200-day SMA at ₹4,217.26 (+5.1% above live CMP), and sell the remaining 30 shares if strength carries to the falling 50-day SMA at ₹4,440.99 (+10.7% above live CMP). On the downside, we ratchet our weekly-close hard stop upward from ₹3,703.75 to ₹3,716.48 (-7.34% below live CMP, matching the live TradingView floor and the 23 November 63-day low of ₹3,716.10). Notice the asymmetry transparently: waiting for a +5.1% to +10.7% bounce risks -7.34% (~₹21,485 incremental loss on 73 shares) if the floor breaks first. That is a 0.70:1 to 1.46:1 trade-off, which is acceptable solely because the ₹3,716.48 hard stop strictly caps downside while giving an oversold tape room to offer a cleaner exit before the H2 revenue step-down and February 2027 promoter lock-up expiry.

Where does the freed capital go once those 73 shares exit? Table 9.3 reconciles 100% of the proceeds. Sixty percent stays in INR broker cash reserve alongside our existing ₹14.21 lakh dry powder, respecting Nifty 50's narrow breadth (55.2% above 50-DMA, 48.2% above 200-DMA). Forty percent rotates into Coforge — an active Stage 2 shortlist compounder trading at 40.4x P/E with +47.4% trailing EPS growth, +3.95% above its 10-week EMA — staged on dips into its ₹1,951.99–₹2,036.18 support zone (stop ₹1,685.64, base target ₹2,620, 1.67:1 R:R). Outside our shortlist, we monitor Dixon Technologies at 0% allocation as the cleaner Stage 2 domestic EMS peer.

One final rule to carry forward: never fall in love with a stock's best quarter while ignoring its balance sheet and chart. Netweb is a real engineering franchise, and if it someday proves self-funding free cash flow, lowers its ₹23.8 crore quarterly interest bill, and builds a fresh Stage 2 base above its 30-week average, we can revisit it with fresh eyes. Today, the disciplined move is clear: zero new money, hard stop ratcheted to ₹3,716.48, and exit all 73 shares on any bounce into ₹4,217–₹4,441.

book_callouts.title: What Would Change Our Mind
book_callouts.text: To move Netweb off REJECTED (TIER_0), three facts must change together: (1) operating cash flow turns durably positive while quarterly finance costs retreat from ₹23.8 crore and GCA falls well below 268 days; (2) order intake absorbs the implied H2 FY2027 step-down and post-February 2027 promoter overhang without margin erosion; and (3) price forms a multi-month Stage 1 base and breaks out into Stage 2 above its 30-week SMA (₹4,556.98) on expanding volume. Until then, protect capital and rotate to Stage 2 leaders.
